source.author: J. R. Childs
source.title: German Military Ciphers from February to November 1918

foreword_evidence.summary: Friedman attributes the report, written about December 1918, to J. R. Childs, with added notes 7 and 12 by other authors. The relevant passage is note 6.

historical_german_reading: UEBER 2 BAYRISCHE GENERAL-KOMMANDO, MUENCHEN: AN 7 RESERVENDIVISION: LANDWEHR REGIMENT; AN FECH: NICHT DURCH KABEL. ARMEESCHLUESSEL DOPPELT. EMPFANG BESTAETIGEN: O.H.L. ROEM. 1 ANR. 11338. GEHEIMORDRE.
historical_english_reading: To the 7th Reserve Division, Landwehr Rgt., for the Director of Railways; via the 2d Bavarian Army Staff: Do not send by cable. Key for the army is a double encipherment. Acknowledge receipt: Higher Command; 1 ANR 11338. Secret Order.

parallel_identification.date_qualification: The p159 copy is dated November 8, while p168 C is dated November 9 and records interception at 21:03. The historical prose appears to refer to the latter copy; it does not explain the duplicated dates or distinguish transmission from interception time.

textual_comparison.assessment: Expanded historical reading repairs two observed letters in the current component layer; the expansion is not a literal equal-length plaintext.
Historical expansion is consistent with a garbled abbreviation, but is not a directly observed spelling.
The historical interpretation differs materially. The current coordinate sequence more closely resembles Landsberg an/am Lech, but exact correction and place-name wording remain editorial.
The historical reading supports the apparent double-transposition instruction while changing an observed W to P.
The historical wording expands a source abbreviation.
The distinctive order number matches exactly; the historical reading expands abbreviations.

cipher_interpretation: The surrounding historical paragraph explicitly identifies a separate double-transposition cipher confirmed by this RICHI ADFGVX message. It does not establish two complete ADFGVX encipherments.
credit_consequence: Order 11338 had a historical reading by 1918 and publication by 1935. The present contribution concerns the p158 composite relationship, explicit source-layer comparisons and repair certificates, not first recovery of this component body.
